node.title: Re^4: unable to eval dumped hash
node.author: jcb
node.doctext:
That way requires a LOT of trust in the safety of [module://Safe].

Perhaps so, but I do not expect that trust to be misplaced. Tcl uses the same concept for its "safe" interpreters and I do not recall any exploits in either that Tcl facility or Perl's [module://Safe]. Do you have a counterexample?

The safe way of saving and restoring data is to handle it as data, not as code.

I agree that that is the preferred option, but interface constraints from existing systems can interfere.
